indicator_definition: This indicator measures the number of persons killed in road traffic accidents per million inhabitants. A person is classified as a road traffic fatality if they die within 30 days of the accident as a result of injuries sustained. Data are compiled by Eurostat from national road safety databases.
rationale: Road traffic injuries are a leading cause of death, particularly among young people. Reducing fatalities requires investment in infrastructure, vehicle safety standards, speed management and enforcement of traffic laws. Progress means a significant and sustained reduction in road deaths per million inhabitants.
methodology_characteristics: Data are compiled from national road traffic accident databases. The 30-day fatality definition was standardised to harmonise counting across participating countries. Data are reported annually to Eurostat and verified against population statistics from national sources.
